printed_page: # P14 (The Protector to Blake and Mountagu, generals at fea, Whitehall 9 June 1656), vol.5
# collectionofstat05thur, leaf 109 = printed p.101, leaf 110 = printed p.102. image_line counts printed
# body-text lines on that page, first line under the running head = 1. Transcribed from
# ciphers/thurloe-printed/images/collectionofstat05thur_leaf0109_p101.jpg and _leaf0110_p102.jpg (IIIF
# native 2374x4047 and native-resolution crops), two passes.
# MAJOR CORRECTION to NOTES.md s.11 item 3 (see NOTES.md s.18 for the full note): that entry, working
# from the djvu OCR alone, concluded P14 has "no separate decipherment line or gloss ... printed" and is
# "mechanical-key-only". The page image shows the opposite: Birch prints a complete word-level
# interlinear decipherment, italicised plaintext phrase directly above (or, on p.101, the cipher-number
# line directly below) its own numeral group, in exactly the same convention as Montagu's other letters
# (P11-13/P15/P17 etc.) -- the OCR simply could not keep the two interleaved type sizes in reading
# order and dropped the small-type cipher-number lines into unreadable fragments. This letter has a real
# decipherment of its own; it is not a mechanical-key application from P11-13/P15.
# Real extent confirmed exactly as NOTES.md s.11 already inferred from context: starts at the heading on
# p.101 (this transcription begins at "GENTLEMEN," for scope) and ends at "in your eye or defigne to be
# done there by the fleet." on p.102 (image_line 22), immediately before the council-attendance
# signature block ("His highnefs prefent, ..."), which carries no cipher.
# Not transcribed (out of this brief's scope, flagged in NOTES.md s.18 and ROOM.md for LANE T): the
# Lockhart letter immediately above this one on p.101 (heading "Chauni, June 19th 1656 [N.S.] ... Will.
# Lockhart") also carries extensive nomenclature-coded numerals (230, 88, 231, 233, 430, 433, 447, 480,
# 351, 100, etc.) with short interlinear glosses of its own ("if my lord protector", "France", "Sweden",
# "Cardinall", ...) -- a possible uncatalogued cipher target, not checked against index.tsv by this
# worker.
